dossier_meta.statement_text: We suspect that the above construction reflects the truth and that $f(n) = 2n - 2$ for all $n \geq 2$.
dossier_meta.context_text: The authors give a construction (attributed to Segal-Halevi [6]) showing $f(n) \geq 2n-2$ for all $n \geq 2$, where $f(n)$ is the maximum number of cuts needed for disproportionate division with $n$ agents. Theorem 1.1 establishes $f(n) \leq 3n-4$, leaving a gap. The authors believe the lower bound is tight and that the truth is $f(n) = 2n-2$.
